q: Find the names of all instructors along with their salary increased by 10%, and rename that column to 'new_salary'.
ans_sql: SELECT name, salary * 1.1 AS new_salary FROM instructor;

q: Find the names of all instructors with a salary between 90,000 and 100,000.
ans_sql: SELECT name FROM instructor WHERE salary BETWEEN 90000 AND 100000;

q: Find a list of all students and the course sections that they have taken. Include students who have not taken any course (using Natural Left Join).
ans_sql: SELECT * FROM student NATURAL LEFT OUTER JOIN takes;

q: Find the names of instructors whose salary is greater than the salary of at least one instructor in the Biology department.
ans_sql: SELECT name FROM instructor WHERE salary > SOME (SELECT salary FROM instructor WHERE dept_name = 'Biology');

schema: PROJECT(Pnumber, Pname, Dnum), DEPARTMENT(Dnumber, Mgr_ssn), EMPLOYEE(Ssn, Lname), WORKS_ON(Essn, Pno)
q: Retrieve project numbers for projects that involve an employee whose last name is 'Smith', either as a worker or as a manager of the department that controls the project.
ans_sql: (SELECT Pnumber FROM PROJECT, DEPARTMENT, EMPLOYEE WHERE Dnum=Dnumber AND Mgr_ssn=Ssn AND Lname='Smith') UNION (SELECT Pnumber FROM PROJECT, WORKS_ON, EMPLOYEE WHERE Pnumber=Pno AND Essn=Ssn AND Lname='Smith');

q: Retrieve all employees whose address is in Houston, Texas (using LIKE).
ans_sql: SELECT Fname, Lname FROM EMPLOYEE WHERE Address LIKE '%Houston, TX%';

schema: student(ID, name, dept_name), takes(ID, course_id), course(course_id, dept_name)
q: For all students in the University who have taken at least one course, find their names and the names of the departments to which the courses belong.
ans_sql: SELECT name, dept_name FROM student NATURAL JOIN takes NATURAL JOIN course;

q: Find the names of all departments where the average salary of instructors is greater than 42,000.
ans_sql: SELECT dept_name, AVG(salary) FROM instructor GROUP BY dept_name HAVING AVG(salary) > 42000;

q: For each employee, retrieve the employee’s first and last name and the first and last name of his or her immediate supervisor.
ans_sql: SELECT E.Fname, E.Lname, S.Fname, S.Lname FROM EMPLOYEE E, EMPLOYEE S WHERE E.Super_ssn = S.Ssn;

q: List all departments along with the number of instructors in each department (using a correlated scalar subquery).
ans_sql: SELECT dept_name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM instructor WHERE instructor.dept_name = department.dept_name) AS num_instructors FROM department;

q: Retrieve all columns from the Orders table, sorted by OrderDate in descending order, and limited to the first 5 records.
ans_sql: SELECT * FROM Orders ORDER BY OrderDate DESC LIMIT 5;

q: Divide instructors into salary grades: if salary < 50k increase by 5%, else increase by 3%.
ans_sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary < 50000 THEN salary * 1.05 ELSE salary * 1.03 END FROM instructor;

q: Retrieve a list of all employees and their department names, including those with no department and departments with no employees.
ans_sql: SELECT E.Lname, D.Dname FROM EMPLOYEE E FULL OUTER JOIN DEPARTMENT D ON E.Dno = D.Dnumber;

q: Find the rank of each instructor by their salary.
ans_sql: SELECT ID, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS s_rank FROM instructor;

q: Find all courses taught in the Fall 2009 semester but not in the Spring 2010 semester (using EXISTS).
ans_sql: SELECT course_id FROM section AS S WHERE semester = 'Fall' AND year = 2009 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT * FROM section AS T WHERE semester = 'Spring' AND year = 2010 AND S.course_id = T.course_id);

q: Calculate the number of days between OrderDate and ShipDate for each order.
ans_sql: SELECT OrderID, DATEDIFF(ShipDate, OrderDate) FROM Orders;

q: Find a three-year moving average of total credits (current year plus two previous years).
ans_sql: SELECT year, AVG(credits_sum) OVER (ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM all_credits;

q: Find all courses that are prerequisites (at any level) of a given course (Recursive CTE).
ans_sql: WITH RECURSIVE rec_prereq(course_id, prereq_id) AS (SELECT course_id, prereq_id FROM prereq UNION SELECT rec_prereq.course_id, prereq.prereq_id FROM rec_prereq, prereq WHERE rec_prereq.prereq_id = prereq.course_id) SELECT * FROM rec_prereq;

q: Find the SSNs of employees who work on project 1 but not on project 2.
ans_sql: SELECT Essn FROM WORKS_ON WHERE Pno = 1 EXCEPT SELECT Essn FROM WORKS_ON WHERE Pno = 2;

q: Format OrderDate as a simple DATE type and round the TotalAmount to 2 decimal places.
ans_sql: SELECT CAST(OrderDate AS DATE), ROUND(TotalAmount, 2) FROM Orders;
